research: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sting — the big con is 'the wire': a crew builds a whole fake off-track betting parlour full of shills, and the mark's bets are placed after the result is already fixed; the film's sections open with old-fashioned painted title cards in a Saturday Evening Post manner with a warm golden glow; muted browns and maroons, ragtime mood, charm over menace

https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/54391 — the chapter cards name the stages of a con (set-up, hook, tale, wire, shut-out), so the card title itself tells the audience which move is being played

https://checkplease.neocities.org/p/40-beats-the-sting — the opening street con is 'the switch': the real money bundle is swapped for a lookalike wad of tissue paper; the fake parlour works as a stage set, a metaphor for the film itself
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_switch_(con) — the switch is a two-person con: a phoney package is exchanged for the one holding the money, so the mark keeps holding something that looks identical

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_game — the shell game is a short con: the dealer moves or hides the marker by sleight of hand and replaces it as required, and shills or a few early wins convince the mark the game is straight
https://cavac.at/cavacopedia/Pigeon%20Drop — pigeon drop: two grifters posing as strangers hand the mark a decoy envelope by sleight of hand while the real stake leaves with them
notes: The Sting's pleasure is that the audience is let in on the trick: we see the crew, the set, the sleeve, the backroom, while the mark sees only the counter. So each staging shows the machinery of the con from the crew's side, with the crew pleased with themselves, and keeps the working man out of the joke (absent, or a small back view in good faith). A: the reveal as an opened hand: both envelopes slit open on the felt, the same order inside each. B: the wire-store backroom: past the curtain, the parlour is a set, one telegraph line runs from both envelopes to a single arms order. C: the shell game with bowler hats: whichever hat you lift, the same crate. Stamps are kept short and exact, the order number is the one repeated element, and every face is under a brim. No film characters, cards, poster or actors; invented notes, no currency marks.
